decision.summary: Vulnerable tenant locked out at night after key snapped in a lock he reported stiff on 22 Sep (R-4766, unactioned). Created emergency JOB-101, assigned the on-file out-of-hours locksmith, informed tenant and landlord, linked R-4766, escalated P1 for ETA confirmation and set a follow-up.

answers.question: Is this tenant-responsibility lockout or landlord lock fault? What is uncertain?
answers.answer: Probably a landlord-responsibility lock fault: the lock was stiff for weeks and R-4766 (22 Sep) confirms it was reported. Uncertain: whether wear or key misuse caused the snap; the locksmith's report decides the recharge. It is not a simple lost-key case.

answers.question: What options do you give the tenant tonight and who pays?
answers.answer: 1) Emergency locksmith tonight (Hackney Locks 24/7): not charged to the tenant tonight; landlord pays if lock fault, recharge only if the report shows misuse. 2) Spare key from office Mon-Fri 9-17.30 with £50 refundable deposit: not usable tonight and doesn't help with a snapped key stuck in the lock. Landlord has approved emergencies without asking and is within spend limit.

answers.question: What actions do you take?
answers.answer: Created emergency JOB-101, assigned Hackney Locks 24/7, linked R-4766, texted tenant, emailed landlord, escalated P1 (ESC-105), scheduled follow-up FUP-104.

conflicts: Policy says out-of-hours lockout is at tenant's cost, but also that a broken lock is landlord responsibility; prior stiff-lock ticket means cause unclear, so the locksmith's report decides, per policy.
assumptions: Tenant's anxiety and cold make this urgent; his SMS is an acceptable channel for an out-of-hours call, with email follow-up tomorrow.
Landlord's emergency pre-approval covers the call-out.

args.body: Hi Jonah, sorry about tonight. We've sent Hackney Locks 24/7 (our out-of-hours locksmith) to 27 Bethnal Green Road, target arrival tonight between 9.30 and 11.30pm; we'll confirm if that changes. Please don't pay them anything tonight. Your lock was reported stiff on 22 Sep, so this may well be a lock fault, which is the landlord's cost; the locksmith's report will settle who pays and nobody will ask you for money before we've spoken to you. If you can, wait somewhere warm nearby, and please don't force the door. The spare-key route (office, Mon-Fri 9-17.30, £50 refundable deposit) is there too, but isn't needed if the locksmith gets you in. If you feel unsafe or unwell, call 999. We'll email you tomorrow with an update.
